flags.name: --library-db
flags.summary: consult another index for calls THIS one cannot resolve.

help: drag-lint index <path>                              [--db <file.sqlite>] [--watch [--interval N]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite> ...]
--library-db (v21, repeatable): consult another index for calls THIS one cannot resolve.
A hit is recorded by qualified NAME on refs.external_target -- never as a call_edges row,
because target_symbol_id is a NOT NULL FK into this db. A LOCAL answer always wins (the
cross-DB rung runs last), so adding a library can never change an edge that already existed.
Answers only when exactly ONE type and ONE member match; absence beats a guess.
WALK SCOPING (any index run): [--exclude-under <dir>]... [--include-only <glob>]...
[--max-file-kb N] [--no-use-ignore] [--no-sql-ms] [--deep|--shallow]
--exclude-under and --include-only are repeatable and prune the walk;
--max-file-kb skips a file larger than N KB. --no-use-ignore opts OUT of the
.gitignore / .hgignore pattern files, which are honoured by default. A folder
holding a .scanignore MARKER file (contents never read) is always pruned with
its subtree; --no-use-ignore does not change that. --no-sql-ms indexes EVERY
.sql file, not just the MS*.sql migration scripts CREATE EXCEPTION text is read
from by default. --deep also records usage refs (--shallow is the default).
drag-lint index --project <file.dproj>              [--db <file.sqlite>] [--recompile|--rebuild] [--dry-run] [--watch [--interval N]]
drag-lint index --scan-libraries-win                [--db <file.sqlite>] [--dry-run]   (Win32+Win64 Library+Browsing paths; alias --scan-libraries)
drag-lint index --scan-libraries-all                [--db <file.sqlite>] [--dry-run]   (every platform: +Android/iOS/Linux/OSX)
drag-lint index --all [--config <path>] [--only <Sec1,Sec2>] [--platform win32|win64] [--recompile|--rebuild] [--dry-run [--json]] [--jobs <n>]
SCAN TYPE is DECLARED BY THE TARGET, not by a flag. --project <.dproj|.dpr>
(or a .dpr/.dproj manifest include) indexes the COMPILE CLOSURE: the project
members, the project-local units they transitively use, each one's sibling
.dfm, its {$I} includes, and the project file -- and NOTHING else. A loose
.pas nobody references, and anything on a Delphi Library/Browsing path, stay
OUT. A FOLDER target indexes the whole tree instead.
MODE is CHOSEN PER RUN. [--recompile] (DEFAULT) updates the index in place;
[--rebuild] first empties it of source, then walks. It deletes ROWS, not the
.sqlite: schema, migrations and settings survive and no open handle is
dropped. Implies --force-reparse. The two are mutually exclusive, and BOTH
apply to index --all: each manifest section honours the mode it was given.
[--force-reparse] (alias --no-skip): re-parse every walked file even when
path+mtime+sha are unchanged. Needed once per DB after an engine upgrade that
extracts something new -- see INBOX 2.3.
EVERY walk SWEEPS, and both halves delete symbols/refs/uses/docs with the
file: PRUNE drops indexed files that left the DISK; EVICTION drops files that
STILL EXIST and left the SCOPE -- a unit dropped from the .dproj, a copy under
an ignored folder, a tree a new [--exclude] now covers. Rows that outlive
their scope make every reference-derived answer (find-callers,
unused-public-symbol, doc facts) wrong. Bounded to the roots THIS run walked,
so indexing one project never purges another's rows from a shared DB, and
reported only when there is something to report. [--prune] forces the sweep
for a single-FILE walk, which does not sweep by default. [--no-prune] is the
one "delete nothing" switch, and it is a DRY LOOK: both sweeps are still
COMPUTED and REPORTED as "would remove" (count + a capped sample of paths),
nothing is deleted. Take it before a big run. Applies to index --all too.
A MALFORMED MANIFEST REFUSES the write (exit 2) -- beside the exe, a local
.drag-lint.json, or --config -- naming the file, the key path and both types
("indexes: expected object, got array"). Read verbs only warn.

entries.title: query --kind --all
entries.summary: Lists every symbol of one kind -- every unit, every class, every enum -- with no name, no doc clause and no row cap
entries.intro: Read this when you need the complete set of one kind of symbol, for example every unit in a project or library index to fill a picker. It lists them all with no name and no row cap.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint query --name <symbol-name> [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive] [--exact]
help: drag-lint query              --name  <symbol-name>  [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive] [--exact]
drag-lint query              --qname <qualified>    [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive]
--name/--qname match CASE-INSENSITIVELY (Delphi identifiers are);
--case-sensitive restores byte-exact matching.
--name also accepts a QUALIFIED name (falls back to --qname on a dotted value).
--exact suppresses the fuzzy fallback, so 0 rows means "no such symbol".
JSON rows carry "match_kind": "exact" | "fuzzy" | "substring" (--name-like) -- reject "fuzzy" unless
you want suggestions; a fuzzy row does NOT carry the name you asked for.
--quiet suppresses the "(loaded defaults from ...)" stderr banner.
drag-lint query              --text "<phrase>" [--any-order|--substring] [--source pas|dfm|sql] [--kind <k>] [--limit N] [--db ...] [--json]
^ searches STRING LITERALS, DFM/SQL text AND COMMENT PROSE (// { } (* *) ///).
--kind literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception
narrows it; --kind literal reproduces the pre-comment behaviour exactly.
searches STRING LITERALS ONLY -- string constants, resourcestrings,
DFM captions, SQL exception messages. NOT source text: identifiers,
property assignments and type names are not in this corpus, so 0
matches for those is correct, not a missing index. COMMENTS: doc
comments ARE searchable -- `query find --doc-contains "<phrase>"`.
Only BODY-INLINE comments need grep. (INBOX 2.7; the old line here
sent people to grep for prose the index already had.)

pitfalls: a project DB IS the compile closure, so a hit is membership and a MISS is non-membership.

STRING LITERALS, DFM, SQL *and COMMENT PROSE* -- // { } (* *) and ///. Filter with --kind: literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception. --kind literal is what this returned before comments were indexed.

help: drag-lint query unit-usage   --unit <UnitName> [--in <file.pas>] [--db ...] [--json]

help: drag-lint lint  <path>       [--rule <id>] [--disable id1,id2] [--rules-dir <dir>] [--json] [--no-preprocess] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>]
[--db <index.sqlite>]  (a store enables the type-aware and ancestry checks)
[--project-rules]  (also run doc-drift/missing-doc for this file -- OFF by default:
they rebuild facts PER DECL, ~16ms each, and can exceed the IDE's 8s budget)
[--stand-in-for <realpath>]  (analyse <path>'s TEXT as though it were <realpath>:

every owning project) without listing them in "autofix" in drag-lint-lint.json;
it also prints "rename-local: <N>" (stderr) for the single-project renames.

entries.title: exceptions-sync
entries.summary: Declare one exception class per distinct raise Exception.Create message, then rewrite the raise sites
entries.intro: Read this when a project raises bare Exception.Create with literal messages and you want one named exception class per distinct message. It runs as a dry run, and --apply writes the classes into a managed block in your exceptions unit; the raise sites are then rewritten by lint --fix.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint exceptions-sync [--db <file.sqlite>] [--config <lint.json>] [--apply] [--json] (materialise the project's derived exception classes)
help: drag-lint exceptions-sync    [--db <file.sqlite>] [--config <lint.json>] [--apply] [--json]   (materialise the project's derived exception classes)
Harvests every bare `raise Exception.Create('literal')` in the project and declares one class per
DISTINCT message inside a drag-lint:auto managed block in the exceptions unit. DRY RUN WITHOUT --apply.
Opt in with an "exceptions" block in drag-lint-lint.json -- an empty one is enough; key "unit" names
the unit (default uExceptionDefinitions, created if absent) and key "root" the ancestor (default Exception).
Each declaration carries its message in a same-line // comment, and THAT COMMENT IS THE KEY: rename a
generated class freely, but edit its comment and the next run adds a second class for the old message.
It is a VERB and not a --fix because its input is project-wide and its output is one file; the CALL-SITE
rewrite is the fix-it half and lives on `lint <file> --fix --fix-rule raise-bare-exception [--apply]`.

--fix [--fix-naming] [--apply]: autofix every unit, as lint --fix (dry run without --apply)
--rule <id>: report ONLY that rule; naming an OFF-by-default rule opts it in
for the run (no --enable needed) -- the same contract as lint and lint-project.
--quiet: suppress per-file progress lines written to stderr

--fix [--apply]: AUTOFIX every fixable finding across the whole project.

batch modes (--unit/--project/document-all) default facts-only: an empty tag is never written, <param> never gets a skeleton, and <summary> appears only when harvested from a nearby // comment; add --stubs to keep a fresh comment that has no facts block
batch modes also skip TRIVIAL Get*/Set* property accessors (impl body <= docs.accessor_trivial_max_lines, default 2) by default; add --include-accessors to document them too
drag-lint document --unit <file.pas> --strip [--apply|--no-backup] [--db PATH]   - REMOVE drag-lint-generated doc tags/blocks (marker-keyed; hand-written docs untouched)
--strip is also accepted on --qname/--project/document-all (strips just that symbol's doc region, or every file in scope); mutually exclusive with --stubs
<seealso cref> links to related symbols (callees + siblings) are emitted BY DEFAULT in every document mode;
--no-seealso turns them off. (--seealso is still accepted and does nothing -- it was the opt-in before it became the default.)
add --since [--base-dir <repoRoot>] to emit a git-derived <since> date; degrades silently when git is absent
@deprecated is auto-detected from the Pascal 'deprecated' directive on the decl -- no flag needed
--migrate-pure: regenerate a stored legacy <para>Pure</para> fact (purity v1). Without it a block whose ONLY difference is that line is left byte-identical, and doc-drift agrees
PROJECT TAGS: on a block reconciled across projects (dl:shared, or holding facts this index cannot see) the inbound entries -- Called from:, Used by:, Used in units:, Covered by: --
carry the projects that rendered them: Called from: [DataCopy,DataCopyTests]uX.Foo (uX.pas). A run adds/removes only ITS tag (the project's name, recorded in the index;
the DB base name for indexes built before 1.18.0); an entry goes when its set empties; untagged legacy entries keep the old rules

entries.title: convert-scaffold
entries.summary: Auto-generates a valid conversion-rules file from the real property trees of a from-type and a to-type
entries.intro: Generate a starting conversion-rules book for a pair of component classes, from their real property trees, instead of typing every rule.

entries.title: lsp
entries.summary: Starts the LSP (Language Server Protocol) stdio server
entries.intro: Read this when you want hover, completion, go-to-definition and diagnostics in an editor other than RAD Studio. It starts the language server over stdio; the IDE plugin launches it by itself, and it is not the same as the MCP server (serve) used by AI clients.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint lsp --db <file.sqlite> (LSP stdio server) [--stdio] [--parent-pid <n>] [--clientProcessId <n>]
help: drag-lint lsp                --db <file.sqlite>    (LSP stdio server) [--stdio] [--parent-pid <n>] [--clientProcessId <n>]
--stdio and --clientProcessId are accepted and IGNORED -- editor clients pass them;
stdio is the only transport, and --parent-pid is the shutdown watch that DOES act.
in lsp mode the engine also listens on a per-user maintenance pipe -- see `drag-lint shutdown`.
--proxy [--delphi-lsp <path>] [--trace <file>]: relay in front of RAD Studio's DelphiLSP,
so registering drag-lint as the Code Insight server keeps the compiler front end.
--trace appends every relayed LSP message to <file> with a direction tag (C>S / S>C); off by default.
drag-lint index <dir> --db <file.sqlite> --resolve-only   (re-derive call edges / ancestry / helpers / purity verdicts from the STORED parses; skips the walk entirely --
the cheap remedy when resolver_fingerprint says the edges are stale, since no parse became wrong)
it writes edges INSIDE this one index only -- no cross-store edges are written (measured
2026-09-22: 0 refs.external_target in every project DB; re-resolving the libraries under
resolver 1.5.1 added 13 intra-library edges per platform, and nothing across stores)
drag-lint index --project <file.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> --resolve-only   (the same, for a PROJECT database -- the form
to type there: without --resolve-only the <dir> form above widens a project DB into a folder DB)
drag-lint index --all --resolve-only   (the same, across every manifest section -- the only command that reaches them all;
use it to repair indexes stamped by a build that skipped the pass, which no later build can detect)

entries.title: shutdown
entries.summary: Ask running lsp engines to close their indexes and stand down, so an index can be rebuilt without killing them
entries.intro: Read this when you need to rebuild an index that running engines hold open: shutdown asks the running lsp engines to close their stores and stand down, without killing them.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint shutdown [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force] (ask running `lsp` engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0)
help: drag-lint shutdown [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force]   (ask running `lsp` engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0)
transport: a Windows NAMED PIPE, never a TCP port -- \\.\pipe\drag-lint-ctl-<sid>-s<session>-p<pid>, created with an
explicit DACL for the creating user only, so another user or session cannot signal your engines. Only an
engine started in lsp mode listens (one-shot verbs and `serve` do not). --all (the default) asks every
reachable engine; --db keeps only engines holding that index; --dry-run lists them and changes nothing.
--wait (default 5 s) bounds the graceful wait per engine: one inside a request answers BUSY and keeps
running (exit 1). --force TerminateProcess'es ONLY an engine that refused or did not answer, and says
ESCALATING when it does. Every honoured or refused request is audited on the engine's stderr and in
%LOCALAPPDATA%\drag-lint\control-channel-audit.log (who asked: pid + exe, when).
